div.style: color: rgb(74, 56, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
separate stores on purpose. One shared lookup and a
customer session would resolve to an agent principal.
The client sends NEITHER customer_id NOR agent_id.

div.style: color: rgb(11, 37, 69) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: services — routes stay thin: validate, delegate

div.style: color: rgb(255, 255, 255) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
every response is a wire DTO (D53)
never CaseBrief.model_dump(). Serialising the domain
model at a permission boundary shipped a real leak:
policy numbers and coverage figures to an L1 call (B5).
Test the RAW BYTES — an assertion on rendered text
cannot see a field the renderer never mentions.

div.style: color: rgb(51, 51, 51) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
GET /health — liveness
GET /docs — OpenAPI

div.style: color: rgb(74, 56, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
D4, enforced by the schema not by a check.
CreateIntentRequest has NO customer_id field, and
extra='forbid' makes smuggling one in a 422. If a
client could assert identity, anyone with curl could
mint a token for a stranger and walk it to L3 on the
next call — the whole ladder would rest on their input.

div.style: color: rgb(74, 56, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
D68: if the server knows it, the server says it.
declarable, offerable, intent_reason, attestation_count,
server_time and what the brief may show are all decided
server-side. The workstation RENDERS permissions; it never
computes them, because a client that decides will
eventually disagree and the client's copy is the wrong one.
